lookalikes.quote: It was named after the Krishna River (also known as Krishnaveni in literature) the third longest river in India. The river flows through the district before it empties itself into Bay of Bengal, near Hamsaladevi village.

lookalikes.title: Ramgarh district
lookalikes.name: Ramgarh district
lookalikes.quote: The district of Ramgarh has been named after the town of Ramgarh, its present headquarters.

lookalikes.title: Ramanagara
lookalikes.name: Ramanagara
lookalikes.quote: It was called Closepet, after Sir Barry Close (1756–1813) in pre-independence times.

lookalikes.title: Ramnagar, Uttarakhand
lookalikes.name: Ramnagar
lookalikes.quote: The town is named after British commissioner Sir Henry Ramsay who established it in 1850 during the British rule in India.

lookalikes.title: Ramtek
lookalikes.name: Ramtek, Maharashtra
lookalikes.quote: Ramtek is first attested in a copper plate grant from the early 400s, during the reign of Prabhāvatīguptā, which mention the place as Rāmagiri and say that they were issued from there. It is later attested in an inscription from Ramtek, dated to the late 1200s, as Sindūragiri and Tapaṃgiri (for Tapogiri, "tapas hill").

lookalikes.title: Ramanathapuram
lookalikes.name: Ramanathapuram
lookalikes.quote: Later the district was renamed as Ramanathapuram to be in conformity with the Tamil name for this region."Ramnad" is also known as "Mugavai"(face) since it acts as the entry point for River "Vaigai".

lookalikes.title: Ramagundam
lookalikes.name: Ramagundam
lookalikes.quote: The city's name derives from a combination of two words, Rama and Gundam. A famous temple of the Hindu god Rama is situated in the old part of the city, where as Gundam means "water springs" are present.

lookalikes.title: Ramnad
lookalikes.name: Ramanathapuram
lookalikes.quote: During the British period this district was called "Ramnad"; the name continued after independence.

lookalikes.title: Sitamarhi
lookalikes.name: Sitamarhi
lookalikes.quote: The city was named in honour of Sītā, wife of Rāma, who was born in Sitamarhi according to Hindu legends.

lookalikes.title: Kalimpong
lookalikes.name: Kalimpong
lookalikes.quote: The precise origin of the name Kalimpong remains unclear. There are many theories on the origin of the name.

lookalikes.title: Kolkata
lookalikes.name: Kolkata
lookalikes.quote: The word Kolkata ( ) derives from Kôlikata ( ), the Bengali language name of one of three villages that predated the arrival of the British; the other two villages were Sutanuti and Govindapur. There are several explanations for the etymology of this name: Kolikata is thought to be a variation of Kalikkhetrô ( ), meaning 'Field of [the goddess] Kali'.

lookalikes.title: Saraswati River
lookalikes.name: Sarasvati River
lookalikes.quote: International Saraswati Festival, organised by the Haryana Saraswati Heritage Development Board (HSHDB), is an annual 5-day international-level festival held in the last week of January in honor of Sarasvati River as a manifestation of Hindu goddess Saraswati, during which the annual pilgrimage along the Saraswati route is organised through various ghats on religious tirthas and Indus Valley Civilization sites.

lookalikes.title: Parvati Valley
lookalikes.name: Parvati Valley
lookalikes.quote: In Hindu tradition, the site is linked to Shiva and Parvati, and its name comes from a jewel (mani) that the goddess is said to have lost in the water.

lookalikes.title: Ayodhya
lookalikes.name: Ayodhya
lookalikes.quote: The word "Ayodhya" is a regularly formed derivation of the Sanskrit verb yudh, "to fight, or wage war". Yodhya is the future passive participle, meaning "to be fought"; the initial a is the negative prefix; the whole, therefore, means "not to be fought" or, more idiomatically in English, "invincible".

lookalikes.title: Vrindavan
lookalikes.name: Vrindavan
lookalikes.quote: The ancient Sanskrit name of the city, ( ), comes from its groves of vṛndā (holy basil) and vana (grove, forest).

lookalikes.title: Dwarka, Delhi
lookalikes.name: Dwarka Sub City
lookalikes.quote: Dwarka is named after the legendary Dwaraka kingdom.

lookalikes.title: Gandhinagar
lookalikes.name: Gandhinagar
lookalikes.quote: The name of the city means "Gandhi's city" and it is named after Mahatma Gandhi.

lookalikes.title: Gandhidham
lookalikes.name: Gandhidham
lookalikes.quote: The city was named after M K Gandhi.

lookalikes.title: Indiranagar
lookalikes.name: Indira Nagar
lookalikes.quote: Indira Nagar may refer to several places in India named after Indira Gandhi: Indiranagar, Mysore, Karnataka Indiranagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka Indira Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu Indira Nagar railway station Indira Nagar, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh Indira Nagar metro station (Lucknow) Indira Nagar, Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir Indira Nagar Assembly constituency, Pondicherry Indira Nagar (Vile Parle) metro station, Mumbai Metro .
